X. C ONCLUSION This paper proves that the reachability problem for checking programs is Ackermann-complete. This lower bound improves the known lower bounds of the reachability problem for many extensions of vector addition systems with states (VASS). Exploited the extra-power of those models to obtain new lower bounds is an open problem. For instance, in [21] we proved that the termination problem of pushdown VASS is decidable in hyper-Ackermannian complexity, but we just have elementary lower bounds for that problem. The techniques introduced in this paper may provide a way to improve the complexity lower bound of that problem, but also the complexity lower bound for other problems on various VASS extensions like the branching VASS and the data nets. IX. C OMPLEXITY C LASSES B EYOND E LEMENTARY The reachability problem for general programs equipped with the bounded semantics provides a way to define complexity classes beyond Elementary. In fact, following [9], the problem that asks, given a 2-dimensional general program M M of size n, whether there exists β such that 0 −→≤K β with K = 1 + Fd (n) is Fd -complete for every d ≥ 3 (see [9] for the formal definition of Fd -complete problems when d ≥ 3). We deduce as a direct corollary the following theorem. Theorem 17. The reachability problem for (4d + 5)dimensional checking programs is Fd -hard for any d ≥ 3. In particular the reachability problem for 17-dimensional checking programs is not Elementary.
